provenance: Corrections to the imported OpenTyria tables in messages.json, from the two sources that can actually arbitrate: our own captures of client build 38797, and the client's own message-format tables recovered from Gw.exe (see studies/msgtable/FINDINGS.md). Kept beside messages.json rather than inside it so that regenerating the imported catalog cannot silently revert a verdict the client already gave us. Applying every entry here leaves zero residual disagreement between our catalog and build 38797's tables. NOTE ON RISK: the codec reads only `fields`; `declared_unpack_size`, `variable_length` and msg_header `length` are metadata it never consults. Of these entries, only GAME_SMSG 140, 146 and 421 change a field list, and Rurik sends none of those three -- so adopting this file changed no behaviour. Its value is that the catalog stops disagreeing with the binary, so later work is not built on a wrong flag. ADDED 2026-08-10: seven GAME_CMSG entries carrying `name` and the evidence for it, from two labelled input runs (toolkit/authsrv/labelrun.py, studies/cmsg/FINDINGS.md). The catalog had field layouts for 194 GAME_CMSG opcodes and names for NONE of them. These change NO field list -- the layouts are copied verbatim from messages.json and already agree with the client's own tables -- so they cannot affect decoding; they record what a message MEANS, which the binary's marshalling types cannot say. In particular 0x0040's u32 typing is correct and was nearly 'fixed' to float: the values are floats, the wire type is not, and the client's own SEND table says u32. ALSO 2026-08-10, later the same day: 0x0040 MOVE_UNKNOWN_FLOATS became ROTATE_PLAYER. That one was settled by the BINARY rather than by a labelled run -- the client's own assertion text names the quantity `rotation` -- and it is worth noting why the labelled runs could not have got there. A labelled run shows you WHEN a message is sent; it cannot show you that an infinity is a sentinel constant loaded from .rdata, and it was the infinities that made an angle look impossible. The wire evidence had been sitting in the vault since 2026-08-04 saying otherwise (every finite value inside +/-pi) and nobody had counted more than twelve of them. ADDED 2026-08-10 (second pass): twenty GAME_SMSG entries carrying `name`, `name_confidence` and the evidence, from a 30-opcode naming pass over the four live tapes of capture 20260807T143055 (10,944 real ArenaNet GAME_SMSG messages, 146 distinct opcodes, framing 100% clean) joined to the client's own dispatch handlers and its 19,620 compiled assert sites. Before this file had ONE named GAME_SMSG opcode of 487; it now has 21. Every entry changes NO field list -- the layouts are copied verbatim from messages.json and already agree with the client's own tables -- so none of them can affect decoding; they record what a message MEANS. `name_confidence` is the POST-REFUTATION value: each proposal was re-derived by a second reader told to refute it, which struck four headline citations and two verdicts. Ten further opcodes came back PARTIAL and are deliberately NOT named here; see studies/smsg/FINDINGS.md for those and for what was killed. ADDED 2026-08-11: GAME_CMSG names from a 20-opcode pass over the CLIENT-TO-SERVER half of the same two live captures. That direction decodes as GAME_CMSG once bit 0x8000 is masked off -- the client ORs it in MsgConn's send -- and it had never been read. GAME_CMSG has no receive handler to disassemble, so the evidence is the SEND SITE plus its asserts, the server's reply within 300 ms (21 GAME_SMSG opcodes are named, so a reply signature is now readable), and a NARRATED session: the operator wrote down what they did, and the map transfers, two kills and two skill casts are all visible in the server's own messages, so the times can be matched to actions. That is a labelled run against ArenaNet's own server. Every proposal was re-derived by a second reader told to refute it, which renamed four and downgraded six. NO field list changes -- layouts are verbatim from messages.json.

2.why: variable_length is false on this build. The binary's own fixed/variable determination is 'contains a type 7 (wide string), type 11 (array length prefix) or type 12 (nested-struct repeat count) cmd'. Our flag is true only because the importer treats `blob` as variable, but a blob is a type-5 cmd -- a fixed `count`-byte payload with NO length prefix on the wire (SPEC section 2; wire-size switch at VA 0x7dcec4 family). 38.name: ATTACK
38.why: Two producers 0x005148B3/0x00514B37 in GmCoreAction.cpp, both containing GmCoreAction.cpp:933 'action < WORLD_ACTIONS' and :934 'AvValidate(targetAgentId)' -- so field 1 is the client's targetAgentId. The six-arm jump table at 0x00514984 sends 0x0026 / 0x0033 / 0x0039 / 0x003F from arms 0-3: four c2s opcodes, ONE switch, ONE targetAgentId, so attack and interact cannot be the same intent. Arm 0 alone is gated on MsCliApiGetMap()==MISSION_MAP_GAME (call 0x0084D9B0 @0x0081668C), fed by the third dword of GAME_SMSG 0x0199. FALSIFIABLE SEPARATION on ArenaNet's traffic: 4 of 5 distinct 0x0026 targets enter a GAME_SMSG 0x00A0 kind-4 auto-attack exchange; 0 of 10 distinct 0x0039 targets ever do; streams with 0x0039 and no 0x0026 contain no combat. Timeline: 17 firings, all inside the two narrated fights, none at any transfer or in either outpost. No assert says 'attack' -- the name rests on switch position plus server behaviour.

57.name: INTERACT
57.why: OBSERVED, studies/cmsg/FINDINGS.md C9. Sent when the operator clicked and then talked to a friendly NPC -- once with the select, three more on repeated interaction, always carrying that NPC's agent id. Clicking a PLAYER produced target-select alone and no 0x0039, so this is about interactable agents rather than about clicking. Evidence: vault/captures/gamesrv/authsrv-20260810T160945-c1.jsonl steps `target_npc` and `interact_npc` (agent 45).

61.name: MOVE_SET_HEADING
61.why: Producer 0x008163A0, sole caller 0x0053547B in the keyboard-walk module (GmWalk.cpp:106 'evt.code < KEYSTATES' @0x0053513E brackets it -- proximity, not containment). The payload is assembled by the AgApi agent-position getter 0x005FC400 (AgApi.cpp:499 'ptr' @0x005FC43F) plus a direction the sender scales by a caller float. The caller dedups: at 0x0053541F-0x00535447 it returns WITHOUT sending when the direction is unchanged -- send-on-heading-change. OBSERVED 430 samples on ArenaNet: |field 3| = 765.0175..768.0000 (sd 1.27) while field 1 wanders -12276..11688, so field 3 is a fixed-length rotating vector and field 1 is a real position. Confirms C5's magnitude constancy, which had only been measured on a harness that could not move.

64.name: ROTATE_PLAYER
64.why: OBSERVED, from build 38797's own binary. Field 1 is an ANGLE IN RADIANS and field 2 is a normalised turn amount in (0,1]. Both are marshalled as u32 -- which is what the client's own SEND table says ([u32,u32], wire 10 bytes), so the typing here is CORRECT and must not be 'fixed' to float -- while their VALUES are IEEE-754 float32. THREE INDEPENDENT LEGS. (1) The client names the quantity itself: the public entry 0x008165C0 range-checks its float argument against the assert text `(rotation >= -1.0f) && (rotation <= 1.0f)` from P:\Code\Gw\Char\Cli\ChCliApi.cpp line 5562, then tail-calls the sender; that argument becomes field 2 (as its absolute value) and decides field 1's sign. There is exactly ONE site in the image that sends 0x0040 -- the 12-byte wrapper at 0x009207B0, found by enumerating all 174 callers of the channel send 0x007DCF00 and recovering the opcode immediate at each. (2) The +/-inf in field 1 is a literal SENTINEL, not a computed ratio: the sender loads +inf from .rdata 0x00948654 when rotation > 0 and -inf from 0x0094E538 when rotation < 0, and when rotation is exactly 0 sends atan2(current facing) with field 2 = 1.0. So an infinity means 'turning continuously, sign gives the direction' -- it does NOT rule out an angle, which is the inference that kept this opcode unnamed. (3) The wire agrees: of 559 samples across 55 game-channel streams, field 1 is never NaN and every one of the 163 finite values lies inside +/-pi (max 3.0190), and 16 of 162 equal atan2(dir.y,dir.x) of a nearby 0x003D direction vector to float32 round-off, 33 within 0.05 rad, against a null model whose 95th percentile is 5. WHICH SIGN IS A LEFT TURN IS UNVERIFIED (121/189 and 106/169 -- real but weak); no left/right claim is made here. CORRECTION TO THIS ENTRY'S OWN EARLIER TEXT: 'field 2 is exactly 1.0 in all 12 observed samples' was true of those twelve and false as a generalisation -- it is 1.0 in 433 of 559, with 105 at 0.425 and a tail down to 0.10133, which CORROBORATES studies/divergence/FINDINGS.md R3 (411/536 and 105 before the 2026-08-10 runs existed) rather than refuting it. The floor is the client's own send gate: it refuses to send below 0.1, and the observed minimum is 0.10133. CORPUS CAVEAT: 536 of the 559 are the harness clicking fixed window fractions, 22 are 2026-08-10 loopback (17 of them tape-loaded), and 1 is live -- so the FREQUENCIES describe our own driver, not a player. The name does not rest on them; it rests on the binary. UPSTREAM ldufr/Headquarter numbers ROTATE_PLAYER 0x0040 independently (GWCA has 0x003E, the known +2 drift); see PLAN.md 6.1 for its register row. Evidence: vault/captures/live/20260807T143055 conn :60935 msg 52 (field1 = 1.08214450 rad = 62.0026 deg, exactly atan2 of the (360.53,678.12) direction the three preceding 0x003D carry), and toolkit/authsrv/test_rotate.py, which re-measures the wire-side invariants every run.

70.name: USE_SKILL
70.why: OBSERVED, studies/cmsg/FINDINGS.md C1. Field 1 is the SKILL ID, not the skillbar slot, and field 3 is the target's agent id. THREE witnesses: the operator named the two skills they cast before any payload was decoded; the client's own skill and string tables resolve 153 and 105 to 'Vampiric Gaze' and 'Deathly Swarm'; and the tape's own 0x00DA SKILLBAR_UPDATE declared the bar as [153, 105, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]. Pressing slots 1 and 2 sent 153 and 105 -- a slot index would have sent 0 and 1 -- and pressing the EMPTY slot 8 sent nothing at all, so the client validates occupancy locally. Evidence: vault/captures/gamesrv/authsrv-20260810T151946-c1.jsonl steps `skill_1`, `skill_2`, `skill_8`.

100.name: CHAT_SEND
100.why: OBSERVED, studies/cmsg/FINDINGS.md C2 and C10. Field 2 carries the typed text VERBATIM, including the channel prefix the CLIENT adds itself: typing `rurik one` sends `!rurik one`. EMOTES GO THROUGH THIS SAME MESSAGE as literal text (`/dance`, `/sit`, `/me waves`), so they are not a separate wire message and /sit is not distinguished from /dance in shape. Field 1 is the current target's agent id for slash commands and 0 for plain chat -- 6 samples across two sessions, two maps and three target allegiances, no counterexample. Evidence: vault/captures/gamesrv/authsrv-20260810T151946-c1.jsonl `chat_say`/`emote_dance`, vault/captures/gamesrv/authsrv-20260810T160945-c1.jsonl `emote_sit`/`emote_dance`/`chat_all`/`chat_me`.

193.name: TARGET_SELECT
193.why: Sole producer image-wide is fn 0x007E6AF0 (two call sites 0x007E6D11/0x007E6D26 -> thunk 0x00816DD0 -> wrapper 0x0091FA30). Its two arguments are named by asserts INSIDE that function: AvSelect.cpp:780 '!(manualAgentId && !ManagerFindAgent(manualAgentId))' @0x007E6B21 and AvSelect.cpp:781 '!(autoAgentId && !ManagerFindAgent(autoAgentId))' @0x007E6B46. Field 1 is the effective selection (manual if nonzero else auto, [ebp-0x20]); 0 clears it. OBSERVED on ArenaNet's own traffic: 75 sends, and every subsequent target-bearing message (0x0039 x29, 0x0026 x17, 0x0046 x4, 0x0027 x3 = 53 of 53) names field 1 of the most recent 0x00C1, never field 2. field1==field2 nonzero occurs 0 of 75, which the je->xor ebx,ebx branch predicts. Nothing target-shaped replies within 300 ms over 75 sends: the server is told, not asked.

10.name: SEND_MACHINE_SPEC
10.why: Builder 0x00491820 has ZERO call sites: it is registered as a connection-established CALLBACK ('push 0x491820' at 0x00491BD9 into the connection factory), guarded to run at most once per process by a four-dword zero test. Every field traces to a Windows API: ole32!CoCreateGuid (resolved by name) for the blob, KERNEL32!GetSystemInfo dwNumberOfProcessors, CPUID leaves 0 and 1 (vendor string; 'and ecx,0xfff' signature), ntdll!RtlGetVersion major/minor/build, GlobalMemoryStatusEx >>20 for MB, and a literal 0x9020 stored when d3d9.dll loads. The frame arithmetic closes to the byte: base -0x238, last field ends at base+0xF0 = 240, matching 'push 0xf0'. Wire checks that could have failed: field 9 == 36896 == 0x9020 exactly; field 5 decodes to a valid 12-byte CPUID vendor string in both sessions; the blob is a structurally valid RFC4122 v4 UUID in both draws and DIFFERS between sessions on the same machine, which kills the machine-fingerprint reading. Fire-and-forget: the client sends its next message in the same TCP flush without waiting. Fields 10/11 (adapter PCI vendor/device) are INFERRED, field 12 UNVERIFIED. Prior art: authsrv.py:111-114 already reads 0x000A/0x000B as the computer-info pair -- that is OUR reconstruction and corroborates nothing; what is new is the per-field API trace.

18.name: REQUEST_QUEST_INFO
18.why: Thunk 0x0091FC00, one caller 0x0080DE09 inside 0x0080DDD0, whose assert ChCliApi.cpp:4253 'context->challengeSortArray.Find(challenge)' sits 18 bytes before the send call IN THE SAME FUNCTION -- the client's word for the argument is 'challenge'. It is a FETCH, not a push: both callers (QuestTaskTracker, QuestChallenge) reach the sender only on the FAILURE branch of a description lookup (0x0080DBE0 = 'test byte [esi+4],1; jne; xor eax,eax; ret'), and the alternative branch is assert(false) at QuestTaskTracker.cpp:299. Reply seals it: GAME_SMSG 0x004C on the same connection in 30.7-61.5 ms with field 1 equal to the requested id, 16 of 16, carrying two encoded strings. Cross-check the corpus could have failed: every 0x003B with code 0x01 is followed by exactly one 0x0012 carrying that id and no other code ever is -- 5 for 5 in each session, both directions. Consider REQUEST_QUEST_DESCRIPTION as the narrower alternative; the reply is a description.

59.name: NPC_SERVICE_SELECT
59.why: Builder 0x00920670 ({0x3B, arg}), sole entry 0x00816340 with 8 callers across GmNpc.cpp, VnLearnSkill.cpp, VnUnlockSkill.cpp, VnUnlockItem.cpp, VnUnlockHero.cpp -- a bank of NPC service windows, not just quests. The argument is a tagged selection id: five call sites OR in distinct high tags (0x0A000000, 0x0E000000, 0x0F000000, 0x10000000, 0x1000<<16) and VnUnlockItem masks with 0xFFFFFF first, which proves the low 24 bits are the parameter. OBSERVED: all 22 wire samples are the 0x00800000 family decoding as 0x800000|(quest_id<<8)|code, and 11 of 11 firings in the narrated session match a narrated NPC action in order, with phase alignment checked at all three map-transfer boundaries. The single code-0x04 in the whole corpus lands strictly between the two Abbey transfers, on the only narrated mid-quest step. Named SELECT rather than DIALOG because 'dialog' is our word and five of the eight call sites are service windows. NOTE: the five OR-ed high tags never appear on the wire, so 'tag+parameter' is established for the code and only the quest family is OBSERVED.

62.name: MOVE_TO_COORD
62.why: Thunk 0x00920720 <- entry 0x008164C0 <- the tail of the walk-module function 0x00535490, which caches a commanded destination in statics 0xC07C2C/30/34 and sends only when it CHANGES. Its counterpart 0x00535570 writes +inf (0x00948654) into those statics and calls the 0x0047 sender instead: cancel the destination, then report position. The asymmetry that settles it: 0x008164C0 passes its own ARGUMENT pointer to the sender, while the 0x0047 entry 0x008167F0 fills its buffer from playerControlledChar via 0x005FC400 -- so this vec2 cannot be the player's position. On the wire the server agrees: 6 of 15 draw an AGENT_MOVE_TO_POINT for the player's own agent 33-65 ms later whose destination is bit-identical to the sent vec2. Was UPSTREAM-only in authsrv.py:664; now confirmed from the client. Field 2 (plane) is 0 in 15/15 live and remains UNVERIFIED on this corpus.

71.name: MOVE_CANCEL_REPORT_POSITION

278.why: variable_length is false on this build. Our flag is true only because the importer treats `blob` as variable, but a blob is a type-5 cmd -- a fixed `count`-byte payload with NO length prefix on the wire (SPEC section 2; wire-size switch at VA 0x7dcec4 family). 421.name: GAME_SERVER_TRANSFER
421.why: Our table stops one field short AND mismarks the message variable. Binary cmds[] @VA 0x00c01b70 (file 0x800b70) is [0x000001a5, 0x00001805, 0x00000404, 0x00000104, 0x00000204, 0x00000104, 0x00000404, 0x00000104]; MsgFormatRecv entry @VA 0x00bcb36c (file 0x7ca36c) statically holds count=8 and the next cmds[] array begins exactly 8 dwords later. Initializer at VA 0x004661d0-0x00466216 copies the statically-present constants [0x00c015a8]=0x1805, [0x00c015ac]=0x404, [0x00c01668]=0x104, [0x00c015dc]=0x204, [0x00c015e4]=0x104, [0x00c01520]=0x404, [0x00c0152c]=0x104. The final 0x104 = type 4, count 1 = a trailing `byte` we do not have: 39 bytes, not 38. No type 7/11/12 field is present, so the message is FIXED, not variable_length.NAMED 2026-08-10, and it is the FIRST name any GAME_SMSG opcode has carried -- the imported catalog has field layouts for 487 of them and names for none. This one is earned the same way the seven GAME_CMSG names were: from a witness that was not consulted to make the claim. It is the GAME-channel twin of AUTH_SMSG 0x0009 GAME_SERVER_INFO. Field 1 is a sockaddr_in for the next instance (family u16 LE, port u16 BE, IPv4 -- the mixed endianness is the client's, and reading the port the other way round is a documented past failure), and fields 2, 4 and 6 are the next instance's world_id, map_id and player_id. EVIDENCE: across the three transitions in one recorded session, every one of those four values equals what the NEXT connection then sent in its own client-to-server VERSION frame -- 12 of 12 fields, parsed straight off wire.jsonl, which the decrypted channel files do not even carry. toolkit/authsrv/tape.py's chain() re-derives that every run and REFUSES a link it cannot prove, rather than ordering hops by timestamp. THE VALUES THEMSELVES ARE NOT RECORDED HERE and must not be: world_id and player_id are live session identifiers from the owner's own account, schema/ is tracked and the vault is not. Field 5 (offset +33) was 1, 0, 1 across the three hops, correlating with destination map 146/164/146 -- possibly an is-explorable flag, UNVERIFIED at n=3 with two of the three being the same map, so it stays unnamed. The 39-byte length this entry corrects is now CORROBORATED by ArenaNet's own stream as well as by the client's tables: in all three tapes the next message begins exactly 39 bytes later.

12.name: CLIENT_PERF_REQUEST
12.why: OBSERVED -- named for what the handler DOES, since the message carries nothing but its header. Its entire body: query GrPerf(counter=4, period=3) under GrPerf.cpp:291/292 'counter < GR_COUNTERS' and 'period < GR_PERIODS', derive a rate, read a global, and send 3 dwords back through MsgConn.cpp:1186. That send computes its wire opcode as '((conn+0x54) ? 0x8000 : 0) | msg[0]' -- which is where studies/divergence D4's mysterious client reply '0x8009' comes from. 79 in the corpus, exactly equal to 0x000D's 79, per connection. PING/KEEPALIVE is not refuted and is recorded as the live rival.

13.name: LATENCY_REPORT
13.why: OBSERVED. The store at 0x0048DA40 discards the value unless it is <= 5000 ('cmp esi,0x1388 / ja'), then memmoves a 36-byte ring and writes the newest sample at its head; the accessor walks up to 10 non-zero samples and returns (latest, mean). A current-and-average pair over a 10-deep ring is a latency graph and little else, and the UiRoot.cpp assert string 's_netGraph' sits immediately before one of that accessor's only two callers. 79 messages, exactly equal to 0x000C's 79 per connection (10/10, 29/29, 2/2, 3/3, 37/37).

30.name: WORLD_SIMULATION_TICK
30.why: OBSERVED. The single largest opcode in the live corpus (3971 of 10944, 36.3%) and it is a clock, not a heartbeat. The client names the one payload dword twice: 'message.time' where it arrives (AgMsg.cpp:208, VA 0x005fcf8b) and 'elapsedMs' where it is consumed (AgTimer.cpp:32, VA 0x00603ff2), and 0x00603fe0 walks a world-scoped timer queue firing everything now due. The wire then agrees on a check it could have failed: summing field 1 across a tape reconstructs that tape's own wall clock, first tick to last, at -1.2 ms over 48 s, -1.5 ms over 147 s, +18 ms over 13 s and +10 ms over 185 s. 445 distinct deltas, 1..520 ms. Rival rejected: HEARTBEAT/PING, which 36% of a corpus invites -- refuted because the payload is CONSUMED to drive a timer queue, not echoed or ignored.

The handler ALLOCATES rather than looks up -- 'mov ecx,0x134; call 0x0047F490' with AgMsg.cpp and line 270 in the operand registers, building a fresh 308-byte object, then asserts AgMsg.cpp:295 'ptr->IsInWorld()' on it. agint.h:929 bounds-checks fields 5/7 as a world position ('pos.x >= worldDims.x0' and its three siblings). On the wire: 416 messages, 416/416 naming an id 0x0020 created earlier in the same tape, 0 naming a never-created id and 0 double-removing without an intervening create -- an all-or-nothing check across the whole corpus.

37.name: AGENT_MOVE_DIRECTION
37.why: OBSERVED, and the discriminator against 0x0029 is the cleanest structural fact in the corpus: this message's vec2 is UNIT LENGTH in 201 of 201 samples (|v| in [0.99655, 1.00000]) while 0x0029's is 1119..21551 world units in 0 of 987. A direction and a destination, not two of the same thing. AgMsg.cpp:412 'syncPtr' and :418 'asyncPtr' show it applied twice, to the authoritative agent and the client's predicted copy. CONFIDENCE IS MEDIUM ON PURPOSE: no assert in this handler names field 1 or field 2; the byte's name comes from the sibling setter 0x002B uses (AgAgent.cpp:2368 '!(facing & ~AGENT_FACING_MASK)'), not from here.

AgAgent.cpp:2301 'm_flags & INTERNAL_FLAG_IN_WORLD' is asserted on entry to the setter the handler calls with field 2, and it tests dword [agent+0x20] -- naming that offset as m_flags. The setter's write is ((old ^ new) & 0x3f0000) ^ new: it KEEPS the old bits inside mask 0x3f0000 and takes the new bits everywhere else, so a server cannot set anything in that mask through this message. AgMsg.cpp:438/443 'syncPtr'/'asyncPtr' put it on the same two agent arrays as 0x0020 and 0x0021. 155 on the wire, 155/155 naming an agent created earlier in the same tape, 151 of them immediately after 0x006D as the create burst's tail.

41.why: OBSERVED, and this CORROBORATES a name the server already shipped as a RECONSTRUCTION rather than resting on it. agint.h:929's four worldDims asserts are applied to field 2 before anything else happens, which settles position over direction -- the exact confusion that makes a rival plausible. AgMsg.cpp:513 'ptr' bounds-checks field 1 against the agent array; the handler builds {x,y,plane,0} and hands it to setter 0x00602a40, which writes the point into the agent's goal slots. 987 on the wire, none unit-length. 43.why: OBSERVED. REFUTES the server's own 'SpeedModifier / modifier, type' gloss: the field is CAPPED at 1.0, so no buff can ride it, and the third field is facing, not a type.

AgMsg.cpp:629/635 syncPtr/asyncPtr, setter 0x00602cc0 asserting AgAgent.cpp:2438. Keep both fields typed dword -- the values are floats, the marshalling is not, exactly as for ROTATE_PLAYER.
